title: FE Fundinfo Extends Nexus for Financial Advisers into Face-to-Face Client Meetings With New Mobile App
summary:
FE fundinfo today launched a mobile app for Nexus for Financial Advisers, opening up its AI-powered meeting support to face-to-face client meetings for the first time.
Nexus for Financial Advisers brings together the data, technology and workflows advisers use across the advice journey in one connected platform, and the mobile app extends that same approach to another part of how advisers work. Information captured during an in-person conversation becomes part of the same connected client record used across the wider advice process, rather than sitting in a separate, standalone tool.
Recorded on a phone or tablet and assigned to a client, the meeting follows the same workflow as a video meeting, including transcription, structured note generation, extraction of client data, as well as adviser review and approval, before information is transferred into Nexus for Financial Advisers or a connected CRM. AI-generated outputs are attributed to their source, while adviser actions remain auditable.
Until now, that workflow stopped at the meeting room door. A significant proportion of adviser-client meetings happen face-to-face, and that data has sat apart from the rest of the advice process, resulting in a gap in an otherwise connected workflow. 
That fragmentation creates a significant administrative burden for advisers. Research from FE fundinfo’s Financial Adviser Survey 2026 found that 95% of advisers say they use too many software applications, and reconciling data between them costs the average adviser 192 hours a year, nearly five working weeks that could otherwise go to clients. 
Christian Wynne, Financial Planner at Factor Financial Planning, commented:
"Nexus and Nexus Assistant have significantly reduced the amount of time we spend on meeting admin. The mobile app means face-to-face meetings will now sit in the same place as everything else I do for a client on Nexus for Financial Advisers, not a separate note I have to catch up on later, but part of the one record I already work from.”
The mobile app forms part of FE fundinfo’s accelerated investment in Nexus for Financial Advisers, with more than 25 new capabilities planned by the end of 2026. The platform combines FE fundinfo’s financial data, research and analytics with AI-powered workflows, reducing the time advisers spend moving between systems and manually managing information throughout the client journey. 
Further developments this autumn include AI-generated suitability reporting, automated client vulnerability assessment, expanded back-office integrations, a consolidated client profile and AI-powered fund research and cashflow modelling. 
Ishaan Sethi, Head of UK Wealth Products at FE fundinfo, said:
“Advisers should not have to change the way they work with clients to accommodate their technology. Whether a conversation happens over video or face-to-face, the information captured should be able to support what happens next without creating another manual process for the adviser. As we continue to add new capabilities to Nexus, our focus is on connecting those individual workflows so advisers spend less time managing systems and more time with their clients." 
NoYesInfrastructure07 Sep, 2026
content: FE fundinfo has launched a mobile app for its Nexus for Financial Advisers platform, extending its AI-powered meeting support into face-to-face client meetings. The new tool allows advisers to record in-person conversations on a phone or tablet to generate transcriptions and structured notes, helping to reduce administrative burdens and connect offline meetings with existing CRM workflows.

Open Banking Delivered by Ecommpay Brings 17% Increase in Payments Settled on Time for Bill Management Innovator – Bill.me
summary:
Working with inclusive global payments platform, Ecommpay, bill management provider, Bill.me has seen on-time payments rise 17% in just three months as a result of adding open banking as a payment option. Across Europe, Bill.me enables its 200,000+ users to receive and manage recurring bills from more than 300 companies and pay multiple bills in a single transaction. The addition of open banking as a payment option has been quickly embraced by Bill.me users, with around 70% of payments now made through open banking in countries where it is available.
Bill.me customers have been paying their bills by card using payment functionality delivered through Ecommpay since 2017. The addition of open banking as a payment option has allowed customers another secure and reliable payment option, and lower processing costs for the business. Customers can now pay directly through any of the major local banks used across Bill.me markets.
The new option allows customers to pay directly through their bank, with their identity verified using Strong Customer Authentication. Secure bank APIs, encrypted data transmission, user consent controls and real-time fraud monitoring help protect each transaction while supporting Bill.me’s security and compliance requirements.
For Bill.me, open banking was not simply another button on the payment page. It offered a way to reduce payment costs compared with card transactions, encourage more people to pay through the app and create a stronger foundation for future growth.
“As we look to enter new territories, the international coverage and scalability Ecommpay offers is critical,” explained Andrey Nemchikov, Chief Operating Officer of Bill.me. “We built Bill.me to make it easier to pay bills, to provide everyone with access to convenient and modern bill management capabilities, and the addition of open banking means it is now easier and more accessible than ever. Ecommpay supports the local banking options our users expect and since launching the additional payment option we have seen an increase payment activity, helping us to deliver greater value to our service-provider partners and future-proof our app.”
“To make its payment experience even stronger, Bill.me wanted to give users more choice while supporting greater payment activity and continued commercial growth,” added Roy Blokker, Head of Strategic Sales at Ecommpay. “Our team worked closely with Bill.me to ensure our open banking solution met their needs and those of their customers. We continue that collaboration to develop the solution as new capabilities become available in future

content: Bill management provider Bill.me has reported a 17 percent increase in on-time payments within three months of introducing open banking through global payments platform Ecommpay. Approximately 70 percent of payments are now made via open banking in supported European markets. The integration reduces processing costs, enhances security with Strong Customer Authentication, and gives users a direct way to settle recurring bills using major local banks.

Miles & More, Currensea and Mastercard Launch Rewards Debit Card for UK Frequent Flyers
summary:
Miles & More, the Lufthansa Group’s loyalty programme, has partnered with Currensea, the market-leading payments technology platform for co-branded multi-bank debit cards, and Mastercard, to launch the new Miles & More Debit Card for UK customers.
Available now, the card gives members a simple way to earn miles on everyday debit spending at home and abroad while enjoying travel benefits across Lufthansa Group airlines. It links directly to customers’ existing bank accounts and works wherever Mastercard is accepted, so there’s no need to open a new bank account, keep a separate card topped up or change the way they normally pay. 
Miles earned through the card can be redeemed for Award Flights, upgrades and other rewards across Lufthansa Group airlines, including Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian Airlines, Eurowings and Brussels Airlines. By using the card, members can ensure their miles never expire, including those they’ve already earned. Together, the Group’s airlines serve 330 destinations in around 100 countries, giving members extensive choice when it comes to turning everyday spending into journeys around the world.
To mark the launch, the cooperation partners are doubling the standard earn rate on UK spend for the card's first year. Cardholders will therefore earn 1 mile for every £1 spent in the UK - matching the permanent earn rate for spending in Europe and the rest of the world, where cardholders will earn 1 mile for every £1 equivalent while benefitting from some of the best foreign exchange rates available to UK travellers. Purchases made directly with Lufthansa Group airlines will earn an enhanced rate of 2 miles per £1 equivalent. Miles earned through card spending can also be exchanged for Points and Qualifying Points once per year, helping members progress through the Miles & More status levels. 
More ways to earn miles with everyday spending
Cardholders can earn up to 15,000 bonus miles in their first year: a 10,000-mile Welcome Bonus after spending £2,000 in foreign currency, plus a 5,000-mile Launch Bonus after their first eligible purchase. The Launch Bonus is a limited-time offer available to the first 500 customers. After renewal, cardholders who spend over £15,000 annually can earn a further 5,000-mile Anniversary Bonus.
Beyond earning miles, further cardholder benefits include priority check-in at the Lufthansa Business Class desk at London Heathrow; an annual Lufthansa Group Business Lounge voucher; 6GB of global travel data; and a one-time 15% discount on eligible Worldshop purchases. 
Gerald Schlögl, Managing Director of Miles & More GmbH, said: “Our vision is to shape loyalty for generations to come. With this new card, we are making Miles & More more accessible to a broader audience in the UK, enabling them to turn everyday spending into meaningful travel rewards. Together with Currensea and Mastercard, we are creating a simple, flexible and rewarding experience that helps members get closer to their next journey with Lufthansa Group.”
James Lynn, Co-Founder and CEO of Currensea, said: “We’re delighted to be working with Miles & More and the Lufthansa Group, the market-leading loyalty programme for one of Europe’s largest airline groups, to meet members in more moments of their everyday lives, not just when they fly. This new card turns the debit spending that Miles & More members are already doing into real progress towards their next trip. Crucially, it does all of this through the bank account they already use. With double miles on UK spend during the launch period and some of the most competitive foreign exchange rates on the market, it delivers outstanding value both at home and abroad.”
Darren Deal, Senior Vice President - Fintech, Government & Digital Partnerships, UKI at Mastercard, said: “Mastercard is proud to support the launch of the new Miles & More Debit Card with Currensea. Bringing together Europe’s largest frequent flyer and awards programme, one of the UK’s most innovative fintechs and Mastercard’s global payments network demonstrates the value of strong partnerships. The result is greater choice and value for UK consumers and a rewarding way to turn everyday purchases into future travel.”
NoYesPayments07 Sep, 2026
content: Miles & More, Currensea, and Mastercard have launched a new rewards debit card for UK frequent flyers. The card allows members to earn miles on everyday spending at home and abroad without opening a new bank account. Users benefit from competitive foreign exchange rates, travel perks across Lufthansa Group airlines, and opportunities to accelerate their loyalty status.
